people.name: Tobit
people.description: Naphtalite exile in Nineveh, known for almsgiving and burying the dead; father of Tobias.

explicit_ages.what: age when he lost his sight

people.identity_note: 14:2 also says his sight returned after eight years. Called "brother"/"cousin" of Raguel (7:2, 7:4); Raguel is "kinsman" of Tobias (6:10).

people.name: Tobiel
people.description: Tobit's father, of the tribe of Naphtali.
people.identity_note: 1:8 calls Deborah "my father's mother" and says Tobit was orphaned by his father.

people.name: Deborah
people.description: Tobit's paternal grandmother, who taught him the tithe laws.
people.identity_note: Mother of Tobiel per 1:8 ("my father's mother"); her husband is not named (presumably Ananiel, but not stated).

people.name: Ananiel
people.description: Tobit's grandfather in the Naphtalite genealogy.

people.name: Aduel
people.description: Tobit's great-grandfather in the Naphtalite genealogy.

people.name: Gabael
people.description: Ancestor of Tobit, father of Aduel.
people.descent_note: Text continues "of the seed of Asiel", i.e. a descendant of Asiel; the number of intervening generations is not stated, so Asiel is not listed as parent.
people.identity_note: Different person from Gabael of Rages (Tobit 1:14 etc.), who is a contemporary of Tobit.

people.name: Asiel
people.description: Naphtalite clan ancestor of Tobit.
people.identity_note: Tobit 1:1 "of the seed of Asiel, of the tribe of Naphtali". Asiel is the LXX form of Jahzeel son of Naphtali (Gen 46:24 LXX Asiel). Mapping is probable but rests on the Greek spelling; reviewer should confirm.

people.name: Anna
people.description: Wife of Tobit and mother of Tobias; a weaver.

people.name: Tobias
people.description: Son of Tobit who travels to Media, marries Sarah, and cures his father.
people.identity_note: Tobias and Sarah had six sons (14:3), unnamed. 14:15 says he lived to hear of the destruction of Nineveh.

people.name: Sarah
people.description: Only daughter of Raguel of Ecbatana, troubled by the demon Asmodaeus; wife of Tobias.
people.identity_note: Previously given to seven husbands, all unnamed, killed by Asmodaeus (3:8, 7:11).

people.name: Raguel
people.description: Kinsman of Tobit in Ecbatana, father of Sarah and father-in-law of Tobias.
people.identity_note: Calls Tobit "my cousin" (7:2) and "our brother" (7:4); not the Raguel/Reuel of Exodus.

people.name: Edna
people.description: Wife of Raguel and mother of Sarah.

people.name: Gabael
people.description: Kinsman in Rages of Media with whom Tobit deposited ten talents of silver.
people.identity_note: 1:14 calls him "the brother of Gabrias" while 4:20 calls him "the son of Gabrias"; the WEB text is internally inconsistent here (Greek recensions differ). Parent link taken from 4:20 only; reviewer may wish to drop it.

people.name: Gabrias
people.description: Relative (father per 4:20, brother per 1:14) of Gabael of Rages.

people.name: Enemessar
people.description: King of Assyria who deported Tobit; Tobit served as his purchasing agent.
people.identity_note: Enemessar is the Greek (LXX) form of Shalmaneser, the Assyrian king of the Israelite deportation (2 Kgs 17). Tobit 1:15 says "Sennacherib his son" succeeded him; historically Sennacherib was the son of Sargon II, so that filiation is NOT recorded as a parent link on the existing ids.

people.name: Sennacherib
people.description: King of Assyria who killed exiles and sought Tobit; murdered by two of his sons.
people.identity_note: Tobit 1:15 calls him son of Enemessar (Shalmaneser); deliberately not recorded as a parent link (historically son of Sargon II). His murder by two unnamed sons (1:21) matches 2 Kgs 19:37.

people.name: Sarchedonus
people.description: Son and successor of Sennacherib who appointed Achiacharus over his accounts.
people.identity_note: Sarchedonus is the Greek form of Esarhaddon (cf. 2 Kgs 19:37 "Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place").

people.name: Achiacharus
people.description: Tobit's nephew, chief officer of Sarchedonus, who supported Tobit; the Ahiqar of the Aramaic wisdom tale.
people.identity_note: Son of Tobit's brother Anael (1:21-22). "Manasses" in 14:10 ("Manasses gave alms, and escaped the snare of death which he set for him") is widely taken as a scribal corruption for Achiacharus (Sinaiticus reads Ahikar there); treated as an alias, not a separate person. Reviewer should confirm.

people.name: Anael
people.description: Tobit's brother, father of Achiacharus.
people.identity_note: "my brother Anael" (1:21); parentage not stated, so no parent link to Tobiel is recorded.

people.name: Nasbas
people.description: Nephew who came with Achiacharus to Tobias' wedding feast.
people.identity_note: 11:18 "Achiacharus and Nasbas his brother's son came" is ambiguous ("his" may be Achiacharus or Tobit); no parent link recorded.

people.name: Aman
people.description: Man raised by Achiacharus who betrayed him and perished in his own snare.
people.identity_note: Not Haman of Esther: this is the treacherous adopted son/nephew of Ahiqar (Nadin/Nadab in other versions). Text: "Aman ... Achiacharus who nourished him" (14:10).

people.name: Ananias
people.description: Israelite kinsman known to Tobit, whose son Raphael claimed to be.
people.identity_note: Raphael, disguised, calls himself "Azarias, the son of Ananias the great" (5:12); Azarias is the angel's assumed name and is excluded, but Ananias himself is treated by Tobit as a real kinsman (5:13).

people.name: Jathan
people.description: Son of Shemaiah, brother of Ananias, a pilgrim companion of Tobit.

people.name: Shemaiah
people.description: Kinsman called "the great", father of Ananias and Jathan.
people.identity_note: Not identified with any Hebrew-Bible Shemaiah.

people.name: the Ninevite informer
people.description: Man of Nineveh who reported to the king that Tobit was burying the dead.

people.name: Raguel's maidservant
people.description: Maidservant sent by Edna to see whether Tobias had survived the wedding night.

people.name: Amos
people.description: Prophet whose words Tobit recalls (Amos 8:10).

people.name: Noah
people.description: Patriarch cited as having married within his kindred.

people.name: Abraham
people.description: Patriarch cited as having married within his kindred.

people.name: Isaac
people.description: Patriarch cited as having married within his kindred.

people.name: Jacob
people.description: Patriarch cited as having married within his kindred.

people.name: Moses
people.description: Lawgiver; "the law of Moses" invoked for Sarah's marriage.

people.name: Adam
people.description: First man, invoked in Tobias' wedding-night prayer.

people.name: Eve
people.description: First woman, invoked in Tobias' wedding-night prayer.

people.name: Jonah
people.description: Prophet whose oracle against Nineveh Tobit believes.

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.description: King credited, with Ahasuerus, with the destruction of Nineveh.
people.identity_note: Historically Nineveh fell (612 BC) to Nabopolassar of Babylon and Cyaxares of Media; the book names Nebuchadnezzar (Nabopolassar's son). Not mapped to the existing nebuchadnezzar id because the text's referent is historically confused; reviewer may merge if the project prefers name-based mapping.

people.name: Ahasuerus
people.description: King credited, with Nebuchadnezzar, with the destruction of Nineveh.
people.identity_note: Not the Ahasuerus (Xerxes) of Esther; usually understood as Cyaxares of Media. Possibly the same Median figure as ahasuerus-dan9, but not asserted.

excluded_names.Naphtali: tribe (1:1,1:4,1:5,7:3 tribe/sons of Naphtali); also part of place name Kedesh Naphtali (1:2)
excluded_names.Ninevites: people (the single informer of 1:19 is entered as an unnamed person)
excluded_names.Aaron: "the priests the sons of Aaron" (1:6) denotes the priestly class, not the person
excluded_names.Levi: "the sons of Levi" (1:7) denotes the Levites as a group
excluded_names.Azarias: assumed name of the angel Raphael (5:12, 6:6, 6:13, 7:8, 9:2); not a human

notes: Text read in full (244 verses). Gabael is two people: Tobit's ancestor (1:1) and the trustee at Rages (1:14 ff.). WEB 1:14 "brother of Gabrias" vs 4:20 "son of Gabrias" conflict. Enemessar=Shalmaneser, Sarchedonus=Esarhaddon mapped; the stated succession "Sennacherib his son" (1:15) is historically wrong and is not recorded as a parent link. "Manasses" (14:10) treated as alias of Achiacharus. Ananias/Jathan/Shemaiah are real kinsmen in the story even though "Azarias son of Ananias" is the angel's cover identity. Unnamed groups skipped: Sarah's seven previous husbands (3:8), Sennacherib's two murderous sons (1:21; = Adrammelech and Sharezer of 2 Kgs 19:37), Tobias' six sons (14:3), servants. Tobit refs include named verses plus key narrative self-references; pronoun-only verses are not exhaustively listed. Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus (14:15) kept as new ids (historically Nabopolassar and Cyaxares took Nineveh). Tobit (Naphtalite) and Raguel are kin, and Tobias is Sarah's nearest kinsman (6:11), but no common ancestor is named.
